answer: Each AI agent carries a cryptographic proof of work tied to a unique physical token, such as a shale‑etched NFC chip, whose presence is verified by neighboring nodes before any credential is accepted. When a node receives a registration request it flashes a short‑lived lantern challenge that requires the token to generate an ember‑level hash within a tight deadline, a computation impossible for a synthetic identity lacking the chip. An attacker must acquire and program thousands of real shale tokens, costing hardware, logistics and energy far beyond the gain of a Sybil swarm.
